Apex Industrial Equipment Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Equipment Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Equipment Inc.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Kevin Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Equipment Inc.'s performance for Q3 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We continued to secure market share gains in high-growth segments while navigating cyclical pressures. Our backlog reached a robust $2.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, providing strong visibility. Operating margins expanded across segments, reflecting pricing discipline and efficiency gains. Lead times improved meaningfully to 14.2 weeks on average, enhancing customer satisfaction. Our guidance assumptions hold firm amid constructive end-market demand. Aftermarket parts and services grew double-digits, now 34% of revenue. Demand trends remained positive in construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing. And revenue grew across regions, led by the Americas.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Equipment Inc. reported $2.85 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 9.5% organic increase year-over-year, excluding a modest FX headwind. Gross margin expanded to 45%, driven by favorable product mix toward premium automation solutions, supply chain efficiencies, and pricing actions averaging 4%. Operating expenses were controlled at $650 million, resulting in operating income of $425 million. Our net income for the quarter was $320 million, or $1.85 per diluted share.

Let me now provide deeper color on several key aspects of our results. Starting with market share dynamics across our key end-markets. We continued executing on strategic priorities, delivering net share gains in high-growth areas while managing headwinds in cyclical ones. Our core portfolio—precision CNC machining centers, robotic automation systems, and heavy-duty material handling equipment—maintains leading positions against peers like Fanuc, Haas Automation, and Kuka Robotics.

Globally, we estimate our market share in the $620 billion industrial equipment sector steady at 7.2% year-over-year per Gardner Intelligence and Statista data. But by geography and vertical, we saw gains of 180 basis points in premium segments offsetting 90 basis points in commoditized areas.

In North America, 42% of revenue, we gained 250 basis points to 12.5% share in automation equipment, fueled by reshoring in automotive and aerospace. Our Gen-4 FlexArm robotic welders, with AI-driven path optimization and 30% faster cycle times, won major deals with Magna International and Boeing, displacing ABB systems. CHIPS Act and Inflation Reduction Act support has grown our IoT-connected installed base 28% year-over-year, with ApexPredict predictive maintenance SaaS at 65% attach rates as capacity utilization nears 85%.

Europe, 28% of revenue, saw 150 basis points expansion to 9.8%, especially in green transition plays. Electrified CNC lines, with 25% lower energy use via variable-frequency drives and regenerative braking, aligned with EU CBAM, securing a €150 million frame with BASF over DMG Mori. We saw mild 50 basis point erosion in legacy hydraulic presses from Italian competitors like Ficep, countered by 15% R&D ramp for hydrogen-ready gear under the Net-Zero Industry Act.

Asia-Pacific, 25% of revenue, held net flat at 6.1%, with 100 basis points gains in semiconductors offsetting 120 basis points losses in general machinery. China competition from Shenyang Machine Tool pressured mid-tier CNC to 4.5% share amid 10% contraction, but premium robots hit 11% in Taiwan and Korea for TSMC and Samsung, with $450 million backlog for wafer fab tools up 40%. In India, we surged 300 basis points to 8.2% via PLI incentives, winning Tata Steel and Reliance with localized AGVs for EV battery plants.

Latin America and rest of world, 5% of revenue, gained 80 basis points to 4.7%, led by mining in Brazil and Chile where IoT-equipped excavator attachments beat Caterpillar in copper bids.

This underscores our Premium Plus strategy: 14% share in digital-native gear versus 3% in legacy. Enablers include $250 million in edge-computing, cutting downtime 40% with ML, and NVIDIA co-development for simulations, plus $180 million German fixturing acquisition. We expect 100-150 basis points FY24 gains, Q4 acceleration in autos and semis, guiding 8-10% organic growth with 45% margins in new wins.

Next, our backlog, a cornerstone for visibility. It stands at $2.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially—our best in five years. Book-to-bill was 1.35x, above our 1.2x target. By segment: Aerospace & Defense 45% or $1.26 billion, up 35% on Boeing and Lockheed CNC orders; Energy & Infrastructure 30% or $840 million, up 22% on GE Vernova turbines and First Solar PV; General Industrial & Automation 25% or $700 million, up 18% on cobots and AGVs.

Regionally: North America 52% or $1.46 billion, up 32% on CHIPS semis and IIJA data centers; EMEA 28% or $784 million on EU Green Deal wind welders; Asia-Pacific 20% or $560 million, up 15% on Indian steel and Korean shipyards.

Conversion: 42% or $1.18 billion in next six months, 75% or $2.1 billion in 12 months, full by FY26 end—accelerating via supply chain de-risking. Enablers: 25% Monterrey capacity ramp with $150 million capex for foundry and cladding, shaving lead times; MachineryConnect IoT on 60% of orders for 92% on-time delivery; dual-sourcing linear guides and rare earths, filling 200 machinist roles.

This positions us for 40% CAGR in EV adjacencies, with backlog margins expanding 150-200 basis points to 28-29% gross via PerformanceGuard contracts at 20% attach. Risks like steel inflation hedged by $450 million cash and low 1.2x net debt.

Turning to operating margin performance by segment, we hit 14.2% overall, up 180 basis points year-over-year and 50 sequentially—sixth straight quarter of gains from pricing, cost-outs, and mix to automation.

Machine Tools, 28% of revenue at $285 million up 12%, margins to 12.5% up 250 basis points: 4.5% pricing, 300 basis points COGS cuts via Smart Factory digital twins boosting utilization to 91%; NA at 15% on CHIPS, EMEA 11%, Asia 9%.

Automation & Robotics, 32% at $325 million up 22%, margins 18.7% up 320: SG&A leverage, rare earth savings for 450 basis points lift; ROS2 software cuts integration 20%; Asia 21% on e-commerce, NA 19%, EMEA 17%.

Material Handling, 22% at $225 million flat, margins 13.2% up 150: freight/steel clawbacks, 88% utilization, lithium-ion forklifts at 500 basis point premium; NA 15%, EMEA 12%, Asia 10.5%.

Power Systems, 18% at $185 million down 5%, margins 11.8% up 100: diesel costs down 8%, hybrid gensets 30% mix; NA 13.5%, EMEA 12%, MEA 9%.

Common themes: 2.5% pricing, 150 basis points COGS deleverage, 60/40 services shift at 28% revenue/25%+ margins. NA 42% sales at 16%, EMEA 13.5%, Asia 12%. Guide FY margins 13.8-14.2%, Q4 from 1.25x book-to-bill.

On lead times for key products and components, weighted average improved to 14.2 weeks, down 18% sequentially and 27% year-over-year—better than peers' 20-26 weeks. CNC centers to 12 weeks via Spartanburg ramp; hydraulic presses 10-12 weeks on $45 million inventory; AGVs/servos 16 weeks via MP Materials neodymium.

NA 12.8 weeks on reshoring; EMEA 15.5; Asia 18. Digital twin with Siemens NX/SAP cuts variability 30%; $75 million capex vertical integration; supplier portal hits 98% SLAs. Boosts NPS to 72, converts $2.1 billion backlog at 95% margins. Q3 stabilize 13-15 weeks, backlog to $4.8 billion.

Key assumptions for our FY24 guidance of $5.25-5.45 billion revenue (8-12% organic) and 22-23.5% EBITDA margins: Global GDP 3.1%, US 2.4%, Europe 1.2%, China 4.7%; PMIs to 51. End-markets: semis 12-15%, aero 10%, EV 20% offset ICE flat, energy stable, industrials +5%. NA 10-13%, EMEA +6%, Asia 7-9%. Smart Factory 2.0 AI twins, 15% capacity, ESG products. Sensitivities hedged by variable costs, $500 million cash.

Aftermarket parts and services hit $852 million, up 12% year-over-year, 34% of $2.51 billion total—15th straight double-digit quarter. Parts $511 million up 14%, services $256 million up 10%, digital $85 million up 25%. Aging base 65% over 7 years; NA $384 million up 15% on IIJA, APAC $170 million up 18% mining, EMEA $213 million flat. Margins 48.2% up 220 via DynPredict on 45% fleet, reman facilities, value pricing. FY24 11-13% growth to 36% mix.

Demand trends: Orders up 18% to 1.35x book-to-bill, backlog $4.2 billion. Construction 35% up 22% on IIJA, utilization 82%, data centers; mining 25% up 28% copper/lithium, BEV pilots; ag 20% +7% precision; manufacturing 20% +14% CHIPS/automation. FY organic 12-15%.

Finally, revenue by region: Americas 47% $1.34 billion +11.4% organic, NA +13% semis/EV, LatAm +4%; EMEA 28% $799 million +5.1%, aerospace/ME upside; APAC 25% $711 million +6.8%, China +4%, India +25%. Q4 Americas mid-teens.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value, with $450 million cash and low leverage.

Now, I will hand over to Maria Gonzalez, COO, for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez (COO):
Thank you, Jordan. Operationally, we've optimized manufacturing processes, boosted supply chain efficiency to 92% on-time delivery, and enhanced customer service through digital tools. We're leveraging Industry 4.0 analytics for excellence and prioritizing employee safety with zero lost-time incidents. Our Monterrey and Spartanburg expansions support reshoring, while Kaizen and apprenticeships address labor gaps.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Kevin Singh, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Kevin Singh (CTO):
Thank you, Maria. We are committed to innovation with cutting-edge solutions. Investments in AI, ML, robotics, and IoT target predictive maintenance, operations optimization, and performance gains. Our new Gen-4 FlexArm robotic welder is transforming the market, with 30% faster cycles, 65% SaaS attach, and major wins driving 28% installed base growth—positioning us for digital leadership.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new Gen-4 FlexArm on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Kevin Singh:
Thanks, Mike. The Gen-4 FlexArm, with its AI path optimization and IoT integration, is a game-changer for automation share gains. Long-term, we see it contributing 15-20% to annual revenue growth through FY26, with 50%+ gross margins from recurring ApexPredict SaaS at high attach rates. It's securing multi-year frames in semis and aero, expanding our premium mix and driving overall profitability up 200 basis points as adoption scales.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

Jordan Lee:
Good question, Sarah. For FY25, we expect 10-12% organic revenue growth, building on FY24's 8-12%. Key drivers: backlog conversion at 75% within 12 months, aftermarket to 36% mix growing 11-13%, semis/EV/mining tailwinds, and regional strength in Americas/India. Assumptions hold with PMIs above 50, hedged against macro risks via diversification.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley (Barclays):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Alex Thompson:
Absolutely, Tom. We're accelerating localization: new Pune plant for India PLI, expanded Monterrey for USMCA nearshoring, Dortmund robotics hub for EMEA. $300 million capex targets 20% APAC mix rise, de-risking China while tapping semis/EV in Korea/Taiwan and infrastructure in LatAm. This supports 9-10% organic growth, share gains to 100-150 bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Maria Gonzalez:
Great question, Lisa. Energy costs up 8% are managed via electrified lines with 25% lower consumption, variable drives, and hydrogen-ready designs for EU tailwinds. Vertical integration and digital twins optimize OEE, cutting usage 15-20%. Reman and lithium-ion shifts add premiums, maintaining 45% gross margins resiliently.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Equipment Inc. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Emily Carter (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
